articles.title: Samsung Android XR smart glasses pre-orders get started on November 12
articles.content: TL;DR Samsung Android XR smart glasses are nearly here, with pre-orders now confirmed to open on November 12. The audio-based smart glasses, developed in collaboration with Google, will feature frames from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. We’re still waiting for details on pricing and shipping dates. Smart glasses are about to enter quite possibly their biggest era yet, with the release of Google and Samsung’s new Android XR collaboration, and now we finally know when you can get your order in. The companies have been teasing these wearables for months now, featuring frames from the likes of Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Last month we heard that a November launch was supposedly confirmed, and today pre-order details are starting to go official. There’s not much to share just yet, but we do have a date: Pre-orders for Samsung’s “Intelligent Eyewear” open in one week, on November 12.
articles.author: Stephen Schenck

articles.title: Instagram's Edits Video Editor is Now Available on Mac
articles.content: Instagram today expanded its Edits video editing app to the Mac . Edits for Mac is intended for larger projects that benefit from a big screen and the control of a mouse and keyboard. The app includes Instagram's licensed and royalty-free audio libraries, sound and video effects, and unlimited automatic captions. Edits for Mac has a full multi-track timeline, keyframes for dynamic transitions, and precise audio waveforms for accurate cuts. There is an option to import LUTs or font files, along with support for Model Context Protocol so AI agents can use the app. The Edits team says splitting, cutting, and trimming are easier. Videos created with the app can be published directly to Instagram or downloaded to share on other platforms. Multiple horizontal and vertical aspect ratios are included, and Edits offers 4K watermark-free export. Edits for Mac can be downloaded from the Instagram website . articles.title: GM recalls almost 70,000 EVs over braking glitch
articles.content: General Motors is recalling some 67,380 vehicles in the US Chevrolet Blazer, Cadillac Lyriq, Vistiq and Celestiq could all be affected Software could be to blame for a temporary loss of braking General Motors has issued a recall for 67,380 vehicles after it became aware of a number of incidents where some of its electric vehicles suffered a temporary loss of braking power. According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) report, GM is aware of 20 minor incidents to date, two of which resulted in minor injuries. In all cases, the accidents have occurred at low speed. Two GM brands are affected by the recall, with the 2025 Chevrolet Blazer EV a particular focus, while three separate models from Cadillac are also included — these are the Lyriq, Vistiq and Celestiq. According to Electrek , General Motors said the issue stems from a software glitch with the brake system control module (BSCM) that can cause a temporary loss of braking while driving under certain conditions. The glitch only affects all-wheel-drive models and owners of the vehicles involved will receive a letter in the mail. Alternatively, VIN numbers are searchable on the NHTSA website , or customers can contact Cadillac or Chevrolet’s customer service phone numbers for clarity. Unlike more serious mechanical issues, General Motors says the software glitch can be patched via an over-the-air (OTA) update or via a local dealer free of charge. In addition to this recall, GM has also issued another for 12,000 Chevy Express and GMC Savana models due to a loose steering gear assembly nut, which could require replacement of the steering gear assembly. Analysis: A simple over-the-air fix (Image credit: Cadillac) While recalls can seem serious, especially when a temporary loss of braking is reported, many modern vehicles, particularly those powered by electricity, can be corrected quickly and easily via over-the-air updates. The software glitch discovered by General Motors is a great example of something that can be ironed out without, in most cases, having to get a dealer involved. According to the NHTSA, Tesla has partially or fully remedied recalls affecting 12.1 million of its vehicles between 2021 and 2025 alone, while most other EV manufacturers are following suit in terms of manufacturing “connected” cars that can receive software updates.
articles.author: Leon Poultney
articles.fingerprint: 000 almost braking evs glitch over recalls

articles.title: Ember’s smallest self-heating mug is on sale for just $33
articles.content: We’ve been fans of Ember’s temperature-controlled mugs for years, though given the price tag, we admit that they’re somewhat of a luxury purchase. Thankfully, if you’ve been looking for a more affordable option, Woot is selling the Ember Cup in black for $32.99 ($67 off) with a 90-day warranty through November 7th. You can potentially save even more as part of Woot’s larger Home and Kitchen Sale , which lets you save an additional $20 off orders of $100 or more when you use code COOK at checkout. Ember Cup (six-ounce) Where to Buy: $99.99 $32.99 at Woot Granted, six ounces isn’t much, but the smaller, handle-free cup is well-suited for cappuccinos, cortados, flat whites, and other espresso-based drinks. It’s also a perfectly fine option if you don’t mind refilling your cup of coffee, cocoa, or tea throughout the day. I’m actually tempted to pick one up myself at this price, especially since I’ve been trying (with varying degrees of success) to cut back on coffee. Like Ember’s larger mugs, the smart cup lets you choose and set your drinking temperature between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit using a companion app, then remembers your setting for future drinks. It can then maintain that temperature for up to 95 minutes on a charge, up to four hours with a lid, or even all day if you leave it on the included charging dock. The cup also automatically enters sleep mode after two hours of inactivity to conserve power. Just keep in mind that, despite its IPX7 water-resistance rating, the cup is hand-wash only.
articles.author: Sheena Vasani

articles.title: openSUSE Leap 16.1 gives Linux users the right to remain immutable
articles.content: openSUSE Leap 16.1 lets users choose between a conventional Linux installation and an immutable system from the same installer, bringing the previously separate Leap Micro into the fold. It's the first point release after Leap 16.0, which we looked at last year when it reached the release candidate stage. Leap 16.1 has arrived ahead of its paid enterprise sibling, SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 16.1, which is expected later this month. Its release notes are already available, and IBM discussed the release in September. The big change in the 16.1 release cycle of both the free and commercial products is that SUSE is merging its conventional Linux with its immutable version, a change the company announced back in February . SUSE previously offered a commercial stripped-down immutable OS, aimed mainly at hosting containers, called SLE Micro . To correspond with that, there was a free community OS called Leap Micro – the final release was Leap Micro 6.2 . Leap Micro is being discontinued as a separate community distribution. The Leap 16.1 announcement says: "Immutable Mode with transactionally updating a system with a read-only root filesystem is a big change for this release. Users who know Leap Micro will recognize it right away, because it is the same approach, now integrated directly into Leap. Leap 16.1 in Immutable Mode replaces Leap Micro, and there will be no Leap Micro 6.3 or 7.0. Users simply boot the regular Leap 16.1 install image and select Immutable Mode in Agama." Both Red Hat and Canonical offer immutable distros, but both use different architectures from their conventional package-based distros. Ubuntu Core is built entirely from snap packages, while Red Hat's "Atomic" immutable distros are built from bootable containers, running on top of OStree , which works a little like a local Git server. Immutable distros built on Arch, such as SteamOS 3 or KDE Linux, resemble ChromeOS at filesystem level, with dual root filesystems that update one another. Leap belongs to the openSUSE family of distros, backed by enterprise Linux vendor SUSE. Its commercial sibling is SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES). Leap is the free, community-supported version, and they are based on the same core packages and release schedule. openSUSE also has a rolling-release version, called Tumbleweed . To rephrase this in terms of slightly more familiar Red Hat equivalents, SLES is SUSE's equivalent of RHEL. Leap is the free openSUSE equivalent of the late lamented CentOS Linux. Leap shares a common core with SUSE's enterprise products while offering a broader community package selection. SLES and openSUSE began sharing enterprise binaries in 2021 . Red Hat, meanwhile, announced the end of CentOS Linux in 2020 , shifting its focus to CentOS Stream. To continue the Red Hat comparisons, openSUSE Tumbleweed is loosely equivalent to Fedora Rawhide , but with automated testing and rollback of problematic updates. Unlike the best-known rolling distro, the entirely community-built Arch Linux, Tumbleweed uses SUSE's Snapper technology to offer snapshots. If an update breaks something, Tumbleweed users can boot into a snapshot of an older version of the OS, before the offending update was installed, and keep on working. If dozens of updated packages a day prove too much, then openSUSE also offers an experimental slower-moving rolling release called Slowroll . Despite the modest version-number bump, Leap 16.1 is a substantial annual update. Its release cycle sits between Fedora and interim Ubuntu releases on one side, and Debian and Ubuntu LTS on the other. Along with its other updates , it brings GNOME 48.8, KDE Plasma 6.6.4, and LXQt 2.4. We tried its Xfce desktop, which surprisingly defaulted to X.org rather than the Wayland-based setup using labwc that we saw in 16.0 last year. Immutable distros look to be the future of Linux for non-technical users. Android is an immutable OS based on the Linux kernel, and sells in the billions – which is why, as we…

articles.title: Nvidia's virtual GeForce 8800 GTX unboxing demo hasn't gone down well
articles.content: Nvidia has a new interactive demo out on Steam It offers a virtual unboxing of a GeForce 8800 GTX… …but you need an RTX 4070 to run it, and the recommended GPU is an RTX 5080 Some gamers feel that it's a 'slap in the face' for several reasons Can't afford a new GPU thanks to the ever-worsening RAM crisis ? Well, Nvidia wants to take you back to the days when a graphics card didn't destroy your bank balance, courtesy of a new demo on Steam where you get to unbox and install a GeForce GPU from 2006. The Verge spotted the interactive demo entitled 'GeForce 8800 GTX — 20 Years of a Legend' which can be grabbed for free on Steam . It was developed by Dylan Browne, an Unreal Engine artist who was commissioned by Nvidia, and the demo is rendered in Unreal Engine (unsurprisingly). The idea is that you can: "Step into a 2006-era PC gaming room, unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX, inspect it up close, and install it in an era-accurate PC tower." On the face of it, that's a rather fun idea — and it's smartly implemented to be fair, including revisiting Windows Vista on a CRT monitor — but if you start to think about it more deeply, this exercise seems more than a little tone deaf in the current PC components climate. Have a watch of Nvidia's illustrative clip below first off, before we move on to discuss this one. Analysis: ragebait, greed, and a lot of other accusations from gamers One of the most obvious sticking points here is the requirements to run this demo. What Nvidia GPU will you need to take part in a virtual unboxing? Here's a clue: it certainly won't run on a GeForce 8800 GTX. In fact you'll need an RTX 4070 at the minimum, and the recommended GPU as per the Steam specs is a… wait for it… RTX 5080. (You must have 32GB of RAM, as well, at minimum). And this comes at a time when the RAM crisis has made that RTX 5080 soar in price to over double its MSRP in the US, and with hefty inflation evident in all countries (over 50% in the UK for example). Don't even start with the RTX 5090, and as we've seen, even lower-end graphics cards are being hit hard with price hikes . As one Redditor put it neatly (with the swearing removed): "A 5080 for an unboxing simulator. They are just laughing in our faces." Another in that thread replies to say: "Ragebait? You are not able to afford a real graphics card — here, take this virtual one?" Speaking of rage, there's quite an outpouring of it in the comments for Nvidia's YouTube video (the one embedded above), such as: "Great job, today consumers have no chance to be able to afford new high end gaming video cards in favor of greed and AI money. A 5090 is $10-15k, and a 5080 is $2k or more — it's a slap in the face to post this tbh." Nvidia has a clear priority for AI, data centers and profits over consumers and gaming GPUs – and it's a business, that's where the money lies, we get that. Shareholders for-the-win and so forth, but given that, the thoughtlessness of this little PR nugget is pretty staggering really. What sort of reaction did Nvidia expect it would get? Okay, there are some Redditors reminiscing about the good old days of 2006, and the 8800 GTX that they owned. However, many more are simply bitter (or indeed incandescent) that Nvidia appears to be reminding us of better times, having done a good deal to cause the GPU pricing pain which is now prevalent thanks to chasing AI profits . While asking for a high-end, now ridiculously expensive, Blackwell GPU to run the demo (at the recommended level). The GeForce 8800 GTX was $599 as a top-end monster GPU when it arrived, and if you want an RTX 5090 these days, you'll pay over 15x that amount. I would think that Nvidia would want to do anything but take a nostalgic trip back to the days of relatively affordable high-end graphics cards at this point in time. Maybe Team Green should have saved this one for the card's 25th anniversary. Will the RAM crisis be over by then?

articles.title: HP’s next CEO loves confrontation
articles.content: The new year will see a new CEO for HP, which after a nine-month search has named Emma Walmsley to lead the company from January 4, 2027. Walmsley was previously CEO of drug company GSK, where she turned around its finances and spun off its consumer healthcare business into a new company, Haleon. She has a reputation for courting confrontation rather than yes-men in the boardroom . HP needs a shake-up as revenue from printing declines and AI-driven demand for components is forcing up PC prices. She will take over from HP’s interim CEO Bruce Broussard, who stepped in in February when former CEO Enrique Lores left the company after more than 25 years to become president and CEO at PayPal. There’s a consolation prize for Broussard, who will become chair of HP’s board, succeeding Chip Bergh who remains a board member. Although Walmsley has been on Microsoft’s board for seven years (she is stepping down in December), this is her first foray into leading a tech company. Her almost 16-year tenure at GSK included more than eight years as CEO, and earlier in her career, she spent 17 years at L’Oréal. Bergh said that during the executive search, she stood out “for the strength of her leadership experience across multiple industries, the clarity of her strategic thinking and her ability to translate customer insights into new growth.” He particularly cited her people-first leadership approach. Walmsley reiterated her commitment to the philosophy in a post on LinkedIn . “HP has an extraordinary innovation heritage, an inspiring purpose and an incredible opportunity ahead as AI reshapes technology and what customers need from it. I’m excited to build on those strengths and help translate innovation into impact,” she wrote. “Behind every innovation are the people who work to make someone’s day a little easier, their work more productive, their ideas possible. In an age of AI, I believe human leadership has never mattered more. It’s a privilege to be joining this team.” Announcing Walmsley’s appointment Broussard said, “We need a leader who can build on our innovation heritage and strengths to boldly shape the company’s future. Emma is a proven CEO with a track record of leading organizations at scale and guiding them through significant change. She has the experience and skills to bring HP’s businesses, capabilities, and people together to capture the opportunities ahead as AI moves to the edge, transforming how we work and live in a more connected world.”

articles.title: Etsy is finally cracking down on AI in product listings
articles.content: Etsy has updated its Seller Handbook to include new guidance on how AI can be used Products must include at least one unaltered listing image that shows the actual product AI can still be used for some purposes, but misleading images will hopefully start to disappear In the wake of Just Eat’s AI generated food image fiasco , Etsy has decided to update its policies to prevent AI being used to generate or edit images, create guides, or use bots to generate listings. The new guidelines , enacted in October, are part of an effort to crack down on images, recipes, and instructions that have been partially or fully AI generated that could mislead customers — and it could help cut down on the torrents of AI slop that have infiltrated the internet . “You, our seller community, have told us you’re concerned about your work appearing alongside items that use AI in misleading ways, and that it’s becoming harder for buyers to recognize your role in creating your items,” the announcement states. “We're taking an important first step to address these challenges.” (Image credit: Etsy) Etsy changes AI usage rules The steps Etsy is taking include changes to how products are physically presented in images, how AI can be used to edit images, and how functional guides are written. For a start, Etsy now requires at least one of the listing images to be a real photo of the actual item being sold with on a real background without any edits or alterations made. But this image doesn’t have to be the first image potential customers will see when viewing your listing. But if you’re wondering about non-physical purchases — such as artwork printed by a third-party — Etsy will allow unedited mock ups from manufacturers for print-on-demand services to be used as the ‘real’ product photo. As for audio and digital downloads, Etsy says the imagery cannot mislead customers. Don’t worry, AI editing is still allowed in some circumstances such as to change lighting and exposure or to resize an image. Backgrounds can also be AI generated as long as the actual product isn’t changed in any way, but using AI to alter the actual product by changing colors, condition, or features of an item is now a hard no in Etsy’s books. Finally, when it comes to other products commonly listed for crafters or cooks, Etsy is changing how they can be written. Written work for instructions, patterns and recipes have to be fully written by the seller with an image representing the real results. So for a knitting pattern or bread recipe, the image must show the finished product. To enforce better detection of AI generated or misleading content, Etsy says it is “investing in tools to better identify authentic versus misleading images and detect and remove listings that use AI to create fraudulent inventory.” The platform is also expanding categories to include misleading AI imagery when reporting listings, which will be used to “help us better understand how members perceive potential AI misuse.” If you are currently using AI generated images for products on Etsy, you still have some time to update listings and won’t face immediate enforcement. The company says it will “provide tips to help you accurately represent your items and meet our photo expectations,” with guidance also provided to sellers with existing AI edited listings.

articles.title: Nintendo says it’s not planning another Switch 2 price hike
articles.content: Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said during the company's latest earnings call that it's "not considering additional changes" to the Switch 2's price, Reuters reports. The Switch 2 got a $50 price hike earlier this year, bringing its starting price up to $499. Nintendo said in Thursday's earnings report that Switch 2 sales have dropped 37.4 percent year-over-year. According to Reuters , Furukawa also gave an update on the RAM shortage, saying, "There has been no major change to the memory situation and Nintendo is in a position to secure sufficient quantities." Earlier this week, one of Nintendo's Switch 2 cartridge suppliers announced … Read the full story at The Verge.

articles.title: ChatGPT can now turn your photos into GIFs — and free users get the upgrade too
articles.content: It seems OpenAI likes to boost its chatbot’s image-generation capabilities at a rapid pace. Just two months ago, users were introduced to ChatGPT Images 2.5 . That update brought faster photo generation, sharper image details, more precise editing, and improved tools for creating & sharing. And now that we’ve reached November, Images 2.5 has officially entered its 2.6 phase. Images 2.6 also promises an even faster rate of photo generation. However, the most exciting aspect of this new update is being able to turn any prompt you can think of or any photo you upload into a GIF. Alongside that welcome feature is the ability to adjust the animation speed of that GIF, edit its individual frames and share the final result across your social media. You’ll be happy to know that the latest ChatGPT Images update is available to all ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users across its desktop, mobile, and web apps. While you’re here, check out some of the fun prompts you can try out with ChatGPT Images 2.6 below. ChatGPT Images 2.6 is here and it’s the ultimate GIF generator (Image credit: OpenAI) I’ve already come across some fun GIF-making prompts, such as “Turn me into a tiny chibi version of myself doing an absurdly enthusiastic victory dance. Transparent background GIF” and “ Create a seamless looping GIF of me in 90s anime style, with expressive eyes, flat cel-shading, and soft colors. Exaggerate my reaction, then ease back to the starting pose. Keep my identity and framing consistent. First ask, ‘How do you want to react?’ and offer emoji choices.” I played around with the new Images 2.6 update myself by trying out some of the best prompts ChatGPT came up with. Feel free to give these a spin so you can turn yourself, your pet or anyone/anything else you can think of into a fun GIF (be sure to upload a photo of what you want ChatGPT to work with first, such as a selfie, a family picture or a piece of art you drew): Turn yourself into a reaction GIF: Turn me into a ’90s anime character in a seamless looping reaction GIF. Keep my recognizable facial features, hairstyle and outfit consistent. Start with a neutral expression, build to an exaggerated reaction, then return smoothly to the starting pose. Keep the camera fixed. Before generating, ask which reaction I want: laughing, shocked, unimpressed or celebrating. Give your pet a ridiculous victory dance: Create a seamless looping GIF of my pet doing an absurdly enthusiastic victory dance after earning a treat. Use a miniature clay-animation style, preserving their distinctive markings and proportions. Keep the background simple and the camera still. Make the final pose flow naturally into the first. Make your own animated sticker: Create a transparent-background GIF of me as a tiny chibi character celebrating a small victory. Give me an oversized head, recognizable facial features and an exaggerated fist pump. Keep the whole character visible throughout the animation, with no text or extra objects. Make it loop smoothly. Turn a doodle into a living character: Transform my doodle into a polished character while preserving its unusual shapes, proportions and personality. Create a seamless looping GIF in which it notices the viewer, waves enthusiastically and returns to its original pose. Use a handmade felt-puppet style, a plain background and a fixed camera. Keep all character details consistent. Build a personalized birthday GIF: Create a seamless looping birthday GIF featuring this person as a charming paper-cutout character. Preserve their recognizable features. Have them blow out candles on a small cake, followed by a burst of confetti, then transition smoothly back to the opening scene. Use warm colors, a fixed camera and no text. Of course, you can tell ChatGPT to make changes to your newly generated GIF with prompts such as “Slow the animation down, keep the camera fixed and make the transition between the last and first frames smoother. Preserve the character’s appearance. ”…

articles.title: Google Home bug is repeatedly asking some users to set up the app again
articles.content: TL;DR Some Google Home users say the app repeatedly asks them to sign in or complete setup whenever they open it. Reports dating back to mid-October mention versions 4.34.22 and 4.35.25.1, although the issue doesn’t appear widespread. No confirmed fix exists, but affected users can try updating to version 4.36.24 or newer. The Google Home app is supposed to remember your smart home devices, but some users say it’s having trouble remembering them. For at least two weeks, the app has been repeatedly welcoming existing users as though they’ve never opened it before, turning a routine trip to their smart home controls into an unexpected account setup exercise. The complaints have been trickling into Reddit discussions and Google’s support forums since mid-October. Instead of landing on their familiar dashboard, affected users say they see a welcome screen whenever they launch Google Home, forcing them to select or set up their Google account before accessing connected devices.
articles.author: Hillary Keverenge

articles.title: Groundcover automates Kubernetes sizing. Engineers set the bounds.
articles.content: On Tuesday, groundcover launched Autonomous Infrastructure in beta to continuously adjust CPU and memory requests for Kubernetes (K8s) Deployments based on production data. Built on technology from Wand, the K8s resource optimization platform groundcover acquired in September , the beta uses data already collected from groundcover’s eBPF sensor to inform resource allocation decisions, while giving engineers a direct view into how those decisions could affect infrastructure costs and workload performance. Shahar Azulay , CEO and co-founder of groundcover, tells The New Stack about the balance the company is trying to get right: “The goal isn’t simply to reduce resource requests as much as possible. It’s to find the right balance between efficiency and stability across the entire environment.” That can mean reducing requests for workloads consuming far less than they’ve been allocated, but it can also mean increasing requests when a workload needs additional resources to operate reliably. The objective is not simply a smaller infrastructure footprint. It’s an environment that continuously receives the resources it needs, without paying for capacity it doesn’t. How to get there? Azulay says teams need “a continuous feedback loop that uses real production telemetry to identify when workloads are over- or under-provisioned and safely adjust them.” Does nobody know a good way to right-size K8s workloads? It’s not for lack of trying. There are already a lot of different ways to tackle the burden of right-sizing K8s workloads. For example, scheduled rightsizing applies changes at chosen intervals, so it may not respond between scheduled updates. In-place resizing can change resources on running pods, although some changes require container restarts. Automated tools can also generate and apply recommendations within policies engineers set. When asked why he thinks K8s rightsizing continues to trip people up, Azulay tells The New Stack the challenge lies in striking the right balance between cost efficiency and application stability: “Resource requests are typically set at deployment time, when teams are making their best estimates before a workload has experienced real-world production traffic,” he explains. “The challenge is that workloads are constantly changing, but resource configurations often aren’t.” “The challenge is that workloads are constantly changing, but resource configurations often aren’t.” After initial deployment, teams may simply let sleeping workloads lie, i.e., they don’t revisit original resource requests for reconfiguration. While workloads may keep spinning along just fine, this approach means teams risk unknowingly leaving them over- or under-provisioned—with costly consequences. For organizations running hundreds or thousands of workloads, keeping those configurations accurate becomes an ongoing engineering task. Teams must analyze utilization, identify opportunities, test new settings, and revisit them as traffic and application behavior change. Even with the expertise, they may not have the time to do it continuously. Azulay describes over-provisioning as “the safer choice because nobody wants to risk performance issues or outages.” But that extra peace of mind can come with unnecessary infrastructure costs; in a 2025 study published in Applied Sciences , researchers found that optimizing K8s resource allocation improved a combined performance-and-cost score by approximately 50% compared to the conventional maximum resource allocation approach. Under-provisioning carries different risks. Requests help Kubernetes schedule pods, and CPU requests influence how CPU time is shared under contention; setting them too low can leave workloads short of CPU time. Limits work differently: CPU limits cause throttling, while exceeding a memory limit can trigger an out-of-memory (OOM)…

articles.title: YouTube bug makes the app appear in half dark mode, half light
articles.content: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube viewers are reporting an issue with using the app in light mode and dark mode. The issue causes the playback area and comments section to be displayed in dark mode, while the rest of the screen is in light mode. Both Android and iOS users are experiencing the bug. Some YouTube viewers are reporting a display issue with the mobile app. The top half of the screen, where the player and comments section are located, is displayed in dark mode. Meanwhile, the rest of the UI is displayed in light mode. According to the reports ( 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ), the bug happens regardless of whether you have dark mode or light mode enabled. Switching Ambient mode on or off reportedly doesn’t have an effect either. Users have tried restarting the app, restarting their phones, clearing cache, uninstalling and reinstalling the app, and adjusting accessibility settings. Despite taking these measures, the effected users claim that the issue persists.

articles.title: Siri AI's Biggest Upgrade Yet + John Ternus's First Apple Earnings Call
articles.content: Apple is finally bringing some of Siri's most ambitious AI capabilities to the iPhone. In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Vlad Savov break down the major changes coming with iOS 27.3, including Siri's new ability to control apps, carry out complex tasks and coordinate actions across multiple applications. They discuss how these improvements compare with AI agents from OpenAI and Meta, and why Apple still has a long way to go. Plus, Mark and Vlad analyze John Ternus's first earnings call as Apple's CEO, the company's strong iPhone sales, concerns about slowing growth and profit margins, and why more price increases could be coming. They also examine Apple's AI rollout in China and the privacy implications of new always-listening Apple Watch features. Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AmneziaVPN's latest update rolls out location sorting to streamline server selection alongside several technical improvements — here's what you need to know
articles.content: AmneziaVPN's latest update adds location sorting, favorites, and a browser proxy for desktop At a more technical level, the update brings log separation, server patching, and design tweaks Roadmap hints at seamless location switching and domain-based split tunneling Amnezia VPN version 5.1.0.6 is now available, bringing location sorting to the forefront of its Premium service. For users comparing it against the best VPN options, this update addresses one of the most frequent user requests as the number of available server locations continues to grow. With over 50 Premium locations now active, the previous flat list had become difficult to navigate. The new version introduces filtering options that let users organize countries by geographic region or alphabetically. Navigation features The latest update places a “Filters” button to the right of the search field, offering two organization modes. Users can group countries by world region – with alphabetical ordering within each section – or maintain a single alphabetical list spanning all locations. A search bar enables quick lookup by country name. Users may also mark up to 15 frequently used locations as favorites by tapping a star icon. This feature works across both the main location screen and the Config Files section. However, favorites are stored locally on each device and tied to the subscription key. This means favorite selections made on a phone will not sync to a desktop computer, though the settings persist through app updates and device restarts. Browser proxy for desktop users Amnezia has also introduced a local proxy option for Premium subscribers using Windows, macOS, or Linux. The Xray proxy runs at 127.0.0.1 on port 10808 by default, routing browser traffic through Premium servers without establishing a full system-wide VPN tunnel. The feature requires the CensorTracker browser extension to function. It operates for a single subscription at a time and automatically stops when the main VPN connection activates. This suits users seeking selective browser routing without affecting other applications on their machine. Additional improvements The update also separates app logs from tunnel logs, giving users clearer visibility before sending diagnostic data to support. Connection handling for Self-hosted servers using XHTTP and XMUX protocols has been refined, alongside fixes for mobile operator connectivity. The Switzerland P2P location now supports bidirectional traffic, with Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) protocols enabled there – handy for hosting game servers , for example. Self-hosted users also gain a one-click button for updating server packages, and some interface tweaks lay groundwork for a redesign due in the next release. What comes next Users can check for updates within the app under Settings > About Amnezia VPN. Desktop installations apply the update automatically, while mobile users can download from the App Store or Google Play. Looking ahead, Amnezia has outlined several planned improvements. These include seamless location switching without disconnection, domain-based split tunneling for desktop users, better stability when managing large domain lists, and more transparent Self-hosted server management. As internet restrictions evolve around the world, tools like Amnezia VPN continue iterating to remain effective. This update signals a focus on usability alongside security – a balance that’s particularly important for users relying on these services for daily access to information.

articles.title: Prevent Siri and Search From Accessing Specific iPhone Apps
articles.content: In iOS 27.2, Apple has a new settings menu that lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one list. Here's what's changed and how to use the new menu. With iOS 27.2, Apple has replaced the old App Access controls with a redesigned Excluded Apps feature that makes it a lot simpler to keep specific apps away from Siri, Search, and suggestions. It's actually a bigger change than it might sound. Previously, excluding an app in iOS meant opening Settings ➝ Apple Intelligence & Siri ➝ Apps and adjusting each app's toggles individually. This included a switch that let Siri "Learn from this App," and several suggestion options that appeared in Search and widgets. What was confusing is that some of these switches controlled on-device personalization, rather than access to an app's contents. Moreover, fully keeping an app's content out of search results also required toggling off a separate "Show Content in Search" switch that was buried in each app menu in Settings ➝ Apps. Thankfully, in iOS 27.2, Excluded Apps consolidates all of this into a single multi-select list, where you can add an app once and make it unavailable to Siri, Search, and suggestions. Here's where to find it. How to Exclude Apps From Siri and Search Open the Settings app on your iPhone. Tap Siri . Tap Excluded Apps . Tap Add Apps , select the apps you want to exclude, then confirm your selection. Bear in mind that excluding an app can disable some Siri features for it. For example, the Electronic Freedom Foundation found that excluding Messages stops Siri AI from reading or replying to messages. Also, onscreen awareness – where you invoke Siri and ask it for information about what you're currently looking at – will no longer work in any app you exclude. Let an App Back Into Siri and Search To return individual app access to Siri and Search, simply tap the Edit button in the Excluded Apps menu, then tap the minus button next to the app in question and hit the checkmark at the top to confirm. articles.title: A device in the White House is apparently using an unsafe proxy — which attackers could use it 'to reach internal systems'
articles.content: Researchers spot White House network traffic being routed through dozens of residential proxy services Findings suggest a device on government infrastructure may have been enrolled in a proxy network Security experts warn proxy services on sensitive networks could enable abuse, anonymity, and potential lateral movement The IT network at the White House was seen routing traffic for at least 28 residential proxy services, meaning there is a strong chance government infrastructure is being abused by (malicious) third parties, cybersecurity experts are warning. Security researchers at Layer3 Intel published a new report , saying they saw 236 instances of residential proxy traffic originating from AS2650. That is the name of an autonomous system registered to the Executive Office of the President, the federal agency that hosts the White House network. The researchers observed the traffic between October 5 and November 3 2026, and said that in 26 of the 30 days of observation, six IP addresses kept appearing. Dozens of proxies “This is public access,” the researchers said. “Anybody can obtain it by signing up to a public residential proxy service, paying a few dollars and sending requests through it.” Residential proxy is a service with a self-explanatory name: paying customers can route their internet traffic through devices connected to residential internet connections (households, essentially), making it appear as though their requests originate from those connections rather than their own. They are not malicious per se, and have legitimate uses, but they’ve become popular among cybercriminals looking to hide their identities, evade security controls, and distribute malicious traffic. Now, according to Layer 3 intel, 28 different residential proxy providers were able to route traffic through the White House network. The researchers cross-checked the IP addresses against public databases maintained by residential proxy detection companies Spur and Synthient, and both identified them as proxy exits. Apparently, the researchers did not set out to analyze the White House’s network. Instead, they said they were testing a newly launched platform that “gives researchers a global view of residential proxy and anonymized internet activity,” and stumbled upon the activity while requesting rotating access through residential proxy services. The cybersecurity community did not seem all too surprised with the news. In a Reddit discussion , IT experts shared their experience with senior leadership, both in public and private sector organizations, saying many were happily sacrificing security for convenience, opting not to install 2FA, or leaving their devices and email inboxes wide open. One reader suspected someone in the White House “probably installed a sketchy free app on their phone, and now strangers are browsing the internet through the building's connection.” The timing of the activity is also worth a mention. Around half of the observed connections happened between 5pm and midnight, Eastern time, with almost no activity recorded during the early morning. Layer3 Intel surmised that a device was regularly connecting to the White House network during evening hours, potentially one compromised by a residential proxy SDK. articles.title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
articles.content: AI Agents now act on the web for millions of people. To a Site, an Agent can take many forms. It may be indistinguishable from a human user carrying out a task, or it might look like one visitor carrying many Users. This removes the ability for the Site to recognize, serve, and hold accountable the user or users behind the Agent, and causes the Site to face the costs when something goes wrong. This post argues that in order for Sites to maximize the access they provide to Agents, the ecosystem must develop new mechanisms to preserve the relationship between Sites and Users. Traditionally, in Security and Fraud Prevention, that requires three things: Identity, Reputation, and Accountability, allowing Sites to answer: Is the person acting being truthful about who they are? Is that person trustworthy? And who answers for the action? “Personal AI Agents” (“Agents” for short) are automations that take instructions from a human (“User”) and pursue a goal by controlling a cloud computer or browser. They are usually hosted and maintained by an “Operator” as part of a managed service or consumer offering. Examples include Muse from Meta and dots from OpenAI, and more are launching all the time. Agents can potentially take any action online that their User could, without the limits that hold humans back. They don't tire, they run around the clock, they act in parallel, and they put up with friction no person would. Much of the web, from how Sites plan capacity to how they make money, assumes those limits. Fundamentally, remotely hosted Agents are intermediaries . An intermediary is anything that sits between a User and a Site, so the Site sees it instead of the User. Agents are the newest kind of intermediary, but intermediaries have existed for a long time. Cloud browsers (hosted browsers that software controls on a User's behalf) and Proxies (services that relay a User's traffic, including VPNs) are intermediaries too. What has changed is the trajectory. Agentic traffic is growing rapidly and may eclipse traditional human browsing on the Internet in the near future. This forces a reckoning for anyone operating a Site today. Historically, a Site could simply block intermediary traffic and require Users to disable the intermediary service. That stops working when the majority of traffic is agentic. Once blocking is no longer viable, Site Operators are left with the problem that intermediaries have always created. The Site loses direct information about the User and must decide whether to trust the intermediary without it. This post covers Agents hosted somewhere other than the User's device. Local agents (e.g. OpenClaw) or Agents running in the User's own browser, on their own device, are out of scope of the primary topic addressed by this post (see below, "On open source and local Agents"). This post rests on one principle: The Intermediation Principle : The business relationship between Users and Sites, and each participant’s security responsibilities, must be upheld regardless of intermediation. A Site needs new tools to recognize, serve, and hold accountable a User acting through an Agent just as it could if that User had visited directly. The Agent, and the Operator behind it, must be recognizable and accountable too, because an Agent can do what no User could. Agents are able to scale human access almost without limit, so they create new risks, even for behavior that was previously benign. The intermediary problem Meet Ezra. Ezra works as a personal assistant for people in her city. Her best client is Amy, a local CEO, but she also works for Bob, Charlie, and Debra. She runs their errands: groceries, appointments, paperwork, and flights. Ezra blends into the crowd. The corner grocer used to know Amy. He knew what she bought and set aside what he thought she'd like. Now only Ezra comes in, carrying orders for four people, and the grocer can't tell whose preferences are whose. He doesn't want…

articles.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
articles.content: Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Create Editable 3D Assets With Houdini and AI Agents Creating animated 3D content requires connecting modeling, simulation, materials and rendering. Nick Scarcella, a senior technical artist on NVIDIA’s BondLab team, directed AI agents — primarily using Claude — to work with CUDA libraries and Isaac Sim to create animations. The BondLab team uses SideFX Houdini and the NVIDIA ovrtx library to develop materials, lighting and the final rendered appearance. In one experiment, Scarcella guided Astra to recreate an OP-1 portable synthesizer using product images, manuals and technical direction. He exported the model into the OpenUSD framework, tested it in Houdini and Blender, then used Astra and Opus to refine details before adjusting materials and textures for ovrtx rendering. Scarcella also used a publicly shared robot-hand checkpoint in Isaac Sim, directing the motion and developing materials and lighting in Houdini with Claude’s assistance. Working with team member Steven Dvornik, the team created an “Echos” visualization: translucent versions of the hand overlap and merge into a single hand animation, offering a visual interpretation of robot training. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Robot_Hand_Video_Omniverse.mp4 Figure: An artistic visualization of simulated robot-hand motion, developed with AI assistance and Houdini’s materials and lighting tools. These workflows bring agent-assisted creation into existing artist tools, giving teams editable content they can inspect, refine and render across applications. Explore Scarcella’s Houdini MCP tools and agent skill . Create an Editable Building Model From Site Scans https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/relay-video-v14-1080p.mp4 Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation. David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes. Wehr guided Astra to interpret panoramic photos, create building geometry and align it with point-cloud measurements. OpenUSD stores the models, while Omniverse’s ovrtx library renders results for inspection. Explore NVIDIA Omniverse agent skills to help agents build with Omniverse libraries. articles.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, and promises this one stays within 'rules of engagement'
articles.content: OpenAI, on Thursday, released its latest cybersecurity-tuned model, GPT-6 Cyber, which the House of Altman says combines "stronger cybersecurity capabilities with better adherence to researchers’ rules of engagement." The new model, we’re told, is much better at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, compared to GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra in early September, and less than a month later, killed off the planned release of GPT-6.1 Astra after the model got better at pursuing tasks but worse at staying within the boundaries of what it had actually been authorized to do. The model maker said the latest cyber model was "trained to stay within authorized scope, respect restrictions and report results accurately." In OpenAI's ExploitGym training evaluation, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5 percent. For comparison, GPT-5.6 Cyber scored 32.1 percent on these same benchmark tests. "In a separate evaluation of whether the model respects the boundaries of an assigned task, it avoided exploiting out-of-scope services over 99 percent of the time," Open AI said. Only 0.07 percent of cases went beyond the intended scope of the training exercise. OpenAI declined to provide additional details about what happened in that 0.07 percent of cases and whether they involved any real-life safety or security incidents - like hacking companies or carrying out supply chain attacks as its earlier models have done during training. We do know, however, that OpenAI recently began denying internet access to the frontier models it is training to help prevent its models from doing bad things. The latest cyber model is also really good at finding and exploiting serious security vulnerabilities, OpenAI claimed. Its researchers used GPT-6 Cyber to find 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox, which Mozilla has started fixing . The model also helped researchers develop working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities , including 588 previously unknown bugs. The Linux findings are being reported with potential patches for maintainer review. OpenAI classified GPT-6 Cyber as “Critical” under its Preparedness Framework . This is its highest-risk tier for cyber capabilities, and means a model can both identify and develop functional zero-day exploits in real-world critical systems, and execute end-to-end cyberattacks. As such, it’s initially only available through the API and Codex to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers - these are customers who are authorized to use OpenAI’s models for offensive security actions such as proof-of-concept exploit development, exploit-chain validation, penetration testing, and red teaming. Over the coming weeks, OpenAI will expand access to all Daybreak Red customers, and is also making GPT-5.6 Cyber available to this group, as well. The model release comes as OpenAI makes a concerted push to improve the security of its products. Earlier this week, OpenAI raised its bug bounty reward payments , and added new bonuses for independent researchers. This includes quadrupling reward-range midpoints, on average, for medium, high and critical findings, so a critical vulnerability in a core product such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API Platform will now earn up to $30,000 - or up to or $51,577 after bonuses - compared to the previous $6,500 payout. Exceptional critical findings on those targets remain eligible for up to $100,000, and now up to $172,000 with bonuses.®

articles.title: AI failures threaten incident management: Here are 4 ways to avoid them.
articles.content: AI is becoming woven into the fabric of digital operations and incident management. On the one hand, AI can detect, triage, and remediate incidents faster, improve coordination between teams, prevent repeat incidents, and drive process redesign. In some organizations, AI is already moving beyond assisting teams to acting on their behalf, as agents pave the way for autonomous digital operations. On the other hand, greater autonomy also introduces greater risk. Unlike traditional software systems, AI-powered incident management tools and agents fail in ways that traditional ITOps and DevOps teams aren’t used to – less predictable and harder to detect. AI has specific failure modes, including hallucinations, groundedness issues, model drift, guardrail violations, or poor tool selection. When these incidents happen, there is often no big-bang failure to set alarm bells ringing. Instead, errors cascade across services into major issues, especially in multi-agent systems. “When these incidents happen, there is often no big-bang failure to set alarm bells ringing. Instead, errors cascade across services into major issues.” The good news is that organizations can mitigate these risks by focusing on four key areas. 1. Deploy guardrails No two organizations are at the same level of maturity when it comes to AI integration. Some are in the adoption and experimentation phase, while others are building ultra-complex workflows with whole networks of specialized agents . The more autonomy an agent has, the further a single bad decision can travel before anyone notices. As organizations’ AI use matures, they need guardrails in place to enforce policy and limit risk. That includes implementing controls to ensure agents stop, self-report, or hand off to a human when they start to drift from their intended behavior. ITOps and engineering teams can then intervene before small problems become significant ones. These controls must contain risk without creating unnecessary friction for engineering teams. 2. Use AI agents to monitor and respond As organizations deploy larger numbers of agents, monitoring their behavior becomes too complex for humans alone. That creates a need for a new layer of oversight in the form of agents designed to monitor other AI systems. By assessing the signals AI systems generate, monitoring agents can identify abnormal behavior and determine when an issue needs to be escalated to a responder. In agentic systems, this responder may not be a human operator, but another AI agent designed for incident mitigation. Almost 70% of incidents stem from changes, so when AI is making changes at machine speed, organizations need to respond at the same pace. “Almost 70% of incidents stem from changes, so when AI is making changes at machine speed, organizations need to respond at the same pace.” Consider a Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) agent designed to investigate as soon as it detects a system anomaly. By the time an on-call engineer is notified, the SRE agent could be investigating, triaging, and diagnosing. Connecting the agent to code, telemetry, infrastructure, and collaboration tools makes those investigations more accurate. Where an incident is a repeat, the agent could also trigger pre-approved mitigation workflows. That provides a pathway to AI-assisted incident management and, eventually, self-healing agentic systems. 3. Identify metrics To know whether agents are behaving as intended, engineering teams need meaningful ways to measure performance. The relevance of each metric will depend on the AI agent and its associated work. However, in general, important metrics include task success (did the agent accomplish what it was supposed to?), groundedness (whether an agent’s responses are supported by the information given to it, or whether it is hallucinating), latency, tool selection, timeout rates, error rates, retry rates, step efficiency, cost, safety and ethical…

articles.title: 7 ways the midterms may affect the AI boom
articles.content: Welcome to AI Decoded , Fast Company ‘s weekly newsletter that breaks down the most important news in the world of AI. I’m Mark Sullivan, a senior writer at Fast Company , covering emerging tech, AI, and tech policy. Sign up to receive this newsletter every week via email here . And if you have comments on this issue and/or ideas for future ones, drop me a line at sullivan@fastcompany.com , and follow me on X @thesullivan . There were 41 ballot initiatives limiting data centers; all but one are on track to pass Voters in 10 states weighed in Tuesday on 41 local ballot measures related to data centers , Forbes reported. Ohio led with 21 measures, followed by Illinois with seven, Maine with four, and Kansas with three. Six other states—California, Florida, Nevada, New Jersey, North Dakota, and Wisconsin—had one each. Of the measures with reported results, all but one went against data center development, reflecting widespread opposition to the facilities. In Ohio, voters overwhelmingly backed restrictions on data centers, including outright bans in several municipalities. More than 80% of voters in Ashville rejected an agreement involving two proposed data centers, though the vote does not itself halt construction. In Kansas, Emporia approved a ban on high-impact data centers, while Ottawa voted to prohibit facilities consuming more than 25 megawatts of power. Boulder City, Nevada, rejected a proposal to permit data centers in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area. One notable exception came in Harwood, North Dakota, where voters rejected a measure that would have required additional review of certain industrial developments, including data centers. Democrats say AI hearings and legislation are coming “Two things will change next term,” Representative Ted Lieu of California, vice chair of the House Democratic Caucus, said at a press conference Wednesday. “We will hold public hearings on AI. We will pass legislation, reasonable guardrails, on AI.” Lieu criticized Republicans for failing to regulate the industry while they controlled Congress and said Democrats would also consider restrictions on new data center construction. The odds of strong AI legislation “just shot up,” Shakeel Hashim wrote in Transformer . He argues that Democrats’ commanding congressional majorities would reduce the need for compromise. If the party wins 56 Senate seats—it currently has 54, with two races uncalled—it would need just four Republicans to overcome a filibuster. Hashim believes that support could be easier to secure as Republicans begin distancing themselves from Trump . Hashim predicts that Congress could within months pass legislation tougher than the bipartisan FRONTIER Act (cosponsored by Jay Obernolte, Republican of California, and Lori Trahan, Democrat of Massachusetts), including mandatory testing and approval of the most powerful artificial intelligence models and tighter limits on federal preemption of state laws. Stocks rallied on the blue wave Trump was supposed to be the president Wall Street and the AI industry wanted. Yet markets rallied on news that he had lost control of Congress. Global stocks initially fell as Tuesday’s midterm results trickled in, then rebounded as the scale of the Democratic sweep became clear, The New York Times reports . The S&P 500 closed 1.6% higher on Wednesday. Asian stocks initially tumbled amid fears that Democratic control of Congress would slow the AI buildout. Taiwan Semiconductor fell 1.5%, while SoftBank dropped 3.2%. But those concerns quickly faded. South Korea’s KOSPI reversed course to close up 0.6%, while European and U.S. stocks rallied. As the Times notes, investors have historically welcomed divided government, and the resolution of election uncertainty can matter more to markets than the outcome itself. articles.title: Major Digital Bank In Paraguay Collapses With Half of Population's Savings
articles.content: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigned Thursday amid mass protests and impeachment threats following the collapse of Ueno Bank, a major digital lender with close ties to his administration and more than 60% of the country's adults as customers. Regulators seized the bank after uncovering risky insider lending and accounting irregularities that left its capital below legal requirements, locking millions of customers out of their savings. The Associated Press reports: Soon after winning its banking license in 2023, Ueno seemed to be everywhere in Paraguay. The digital lender, a rebranded version of a decades-old finance company, lured customers with generous cash-back offers on groceries, grew to more than 70 locations, sponsored Paraguay's national soccer team and plastered its name on the country's main stadium. Government money poured into Ueno's coffers under Pena. He also appointed Carlos Carvallo, president of Financiera Ueno, the predecessor to Ueno Bank, to run the central bank, the agency charged with supervising the digital lender. As of last month, Ueno reported holding roughly $800 million in public deposits, about a quarter of its total, including money from the state pension and health fund and the operators of Paraguay's giant hydroelectric dams. Even as retirees' savings and other public money piled up at Ueno, worries were escalating inside the central bank. In June, its inspectors found a pattern of risky lending to insiders, reported ABC Color, a leading Paraguayan newspaper. Ueno had extended large sums to companies tied to its owners, beyond what the law allows and without enough collateral to cover the debts if they went bad. On a single day in September 2025, nearly $39 million had gone to three such companies. Pena repeatedly brushed off the warnings. As recently as last month, he defended Ueno and the central bank's oversight, dismissing the concerns as a smear campaign that was spooking the public. But on Monday, it all came crashing down. Regulators investigating Ueno's loans to companies linked to its owners found poorly documented lending, the central bank said, as well as expenses the bank had wrongly counted as assets. Once the books were corrected, Ueno's capital, the cushion banks must keep to absorb losses, fell to less than half the legal minimum. The central bank seized the lender Tuesday and announced plans to move customers' accounts, along with whatever assets still hold value, to other banks before liquidating what's left. Ueno's app, cards and transfers went dark and its branches locked their doors, leaving desperate depositors lined up outside with no way to cash out their savings. On Wednesday, a rush to open new accounts elsewhere crashed other banks' mobile apps, fueling public panic. Officials say they had begun repaying depositors and opening accounts at other banks for the roughly 280,000 customers who had banked exclusively with Ueno. "The banking system is sound," insisted Pedro Acosta Bernal, appointed interim central bank president Wednesday after Carvallo resigned at Pena's request. Meanwhile, eight senior Ueno executives have been detained, including founder Miguel Vazquez and bank President Juan Manuel Gustale. "Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud," reports the AP. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: ExpressVPN makes its AI assistant and tracker blocking available to all users
articles.content: ExpressVPN has added tracker blocking to its Basic plan, a tool previously limited to Advanced and Pro plans ExpressAI is also now included with 50 daily credits, 1 model, and 100MB of storage The change follows the February 2026 shift to three plans offering its new spread of tools ExpressVPN has expanded what its entry-level Basic plan includes, adding two features that were previously reserved for higher-priced tiers. Subscribers on Basic now get tracker blocking alongside access to ExpressAI, the company’s private AI assistant. Until now, that level of protection started with the Advanced plan, while ExpressAI was exclusive to Pro. Here’s what’s changed, and why it matters. Tracker blocking comes to Basic The Basic plan already blocked ads, malicious sites, and adult content – a package ExpressVPN calls Lite Protection. It lacked tracker blocking: the ability to stop scripts that follow you around the web and quietly build a profile of what you browse. That capability used to start at the Advanced tier but is now part of Basic. For a plan that already sits at the cheaper end of the market, at just $2.99/month, that narrows the gap between budget and mid-tier subscriptions considerably. Advanced keeps its other perks – 12 simultaneous connections versus Basic’s 10 and a more generous email protection allowance. ExpressAI arrives on the lower tiers The bigger addition is ExpressAI , a private AI assistant built on confidential computing. In plain terms, that means conversations are processed inside a protected environment that even the provider itself can’t read – a pointed answer to the growing unease over how much consumer AI chatbots actually see. Basic subscribers get 50 credits a day, 1 AI model, and 100MB of storage, with web search included. Advanced bumps that to 100 credits daily, the same single model, and 500MB of storage. Pro – still the home for power users – retains the fullest version, with 500 credits per day, six AI models, and 2GB of storage. Whether 50 credits and 100MB is enough depends on how heavily you lean on an assistant; it’s best thought of as a taste of the full service rather than a replacement for it. Yet for anyone curious about private AI who was put off by the Pro price, there’s now a much lower barrier to entry. Part of a bigger push The update extends a strategy ExpressVPN kicked off in February 2026 , when it rebuilt its plan lineup around a suite of tools: the ExpressAI assistant, the ExpressMailGuard email shield and the Identity Defender monitoring service, which was limited to US users at launch. ExpressKeys , the provider’s password manager , moved from the main app to a standalone one as part of the same shake-up. At the time, TechRadar’s Rob Dunne called the restructure “the biggest expansion to ExpressVPN’s portfolio since its eSIM launched in December 2024.” Even then, Basic users missed out on much of it – no ExpressKeys, no Identity Defender, and no tracker blocking either. That’s what makes the current update notable. With Black Friday landing on November 27, VPN providers are already dangling enticing offers: Surfshark was one of the first out of the blocks, dropping the price of its mid-tier plan to match its entry-level one. Against that backdrop, ExpressVPN’s richer Basic plan looks well positioned for the sales season.

articles.title: Chinese AI lab Moonshot reportedly looked at European data centers to access Nvidia chips, report claims
articles.content: Moonshot AI, the Chinese lab that made Kimi, is reportedly looking towards Europe to gain access to the latest Nvidia Blackwell AI GPUs. According to CNBC , the company is in talks with at least one European data center to lease clusters with 8,000 or more GPUs for inferencing, and that it’s also interested in securing compute capacity for training. Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible While Chinese companies are banned from acquiring Nvidia Blackwell and other AI GPUs that offer the same or better performance containing U.S. technologies, a loophole has so far allowed them to gain access to compute by renting them from data centers abroad. The U.S. House is attempting to patch it and passed the Remote Access Security Act , but it must still go through the Senate and the White House before it can turn into law. In the meantime, Chinese AI labs are exploiting the loophole and training their models on foreign data centers that have acquired Nvidia chips. The U.S. and China have been locked in an AI arms race, with the latter’s open-weight models behind frontier U.S. models by just a matter of months . More importantly, these models, like Kimi K3, are significantly easier to run and could even be much cheaper to use . These advancements happened despite Washington’s efforts to make it harder for Chinese AI labs to acquire hardware that uses American technologies through export bans. But even though President Donald Trump eventually made a 180-degree turn and allowed Nvidia H200 chips for export to China , Beijing has taken steps to protect its domestic AI chip industry by blocking H200 imports at the border, meaning these companies must look elsewhere if they want to access the latest, most powerful AI GPUs to train their models. Moonshot also has a limited window if it wants to secure compute capacity outside of China — Nvidia has reportedly told its data center clients to limit their business and avoid serving more than 49% of their capacity to Chinese outfits . This could be a harbinger of things to come, especially as reports like these could spotlight the bipartisan bill and increase pressure to advance the legislation sooner rather than later.
articles.author: Jowi Morales

articles.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 is here, and it can turn your photos into animated GIFs
articles.content: OpenAI has just released ChatGPT Images 2.6 across all subscription levels, including Free. It’s only a 0.1 upgrade to the previous Images 2.5 , so it should come as no surprise that not that much has changed. In fact, there are only two new features, but they’re both worth your attention. Firstly, you can now use ChatGPT to make animated GIF images, and second, you can now upload a persistent reference image, so you don’t need to keep uploading it when requesting a lot of different edits. The first change is perhaps the most immediately interesting, but the second one could become more useful in the long run. More cat GIFs, please The Internet can never have enough cat GIFs, so naturally I decided to try the new feature on a photo of my cat, Chester. While Halloween has just been and gone, I thought I’d use that as inspiration for the sort of image I wanted to make of my cat. I used a fairly simple prompt: “Can you make a Halloween GIF of my cat to share with family?” ChatGPT obliged without any objection, and transformed my cat into a feline wearing a Halloween-themed hat and cape and blinking slowly as a pumpkin flickered in the background. It’s especially fun for my family because there’s no way he’d ever let a human dress him up like this. Once you’ve created your GIF it gives you a shareable link, so you don’t need to host it anywhere if you want to link people to it. Alternatively, you can download it or share it straight to X, LinkedIn and Reddit. (Image credit: OpenAI / Graham Barlow) What ChatGPT produced was ok, but it was hardly going to set the Internet on fire, so I followed up with “That's cool, but it's not very active, can you make it more active please? Get creative.” “Now we're talking!”, replied ChatGPT. “Your cat's gone full witch mode — casting a spell with a raised paw, conjuring a floating, glowing pumpkin, then giving a triumphant little meow before licking their lips. A proper bit of Halloween mischief!” (Image credit: OpenAI / Graham Barlow) Indeed, the resulting GIF was much better, and Chester's movements looked realistic. I think this shows how important your prompt writing is — don’t be afraid to ask ChatGPT to get creative. Time and time again Of course, I might want to produce a GIF of this photo for a different occasion in the future so I asked ChatGPT: “ Can you save the original photo as Chester so I can reference it again?” After thinking for a second, it saved the photo as a reference image called Chester. It made a point that it was saving the original snap, not the Halloween versions, and said “In future chats, you can simply say something like: ‘Create a picture of @Chester dressed as a pirate.’ And I'll be able to use his original appearance without you needing to upload the photo again.” I tested it with the prompt “Make a GIF of @Chester on the moon” and it provided one of Chester as an astronaut chasing a butterfly. How the butterfly was surviving on the moon, and how Chester was surviving when his ears poked through his space helmet, I don’t know, but I’ll go with it anyway. (Image credit: OpenAI / Graham Barlow) Saving a reference image is a genuinely useful new feature. It might not be as flashy as the GIF creation, but I think it’s going to come in handy for the future. Overall I’m pretty happy with the Images 2.6 update. Nothing major has changed, but it’s nice to know I can now create a GIF from an image whenever I want, using ChatGPT’s natural language input method. The best thing about Images 2.6 is how little effort it takes to get something fun out of it. I didn't need animation software, any technical knowledge or even a particularly clever prompt. All I needed was a picture of my cat and a willingness to let ChatGPT get creative. And now that Chester is saved as a reference image, I suspect this won't be his last starring role.

articles.title: Copilot Chat has usage caps, and Microsoft would rather you found them by hitting them
articles.content: Microsoft is applying usage limits to more Copilot Chat features for commercial users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and it won't publish the numerical caps. Copilot Chat comes with qualifying Microsoft 365 business and enterprise subscriptions. Without the Copilot add-on, it can reason over web information and uploaded files. The paid license adds broader access to work data, including emails, meetings, chats, and documents. Tasks already in progress won't be interrupted. Once a limit is reached, users will receive an in-product notice explaining when to retry the affected feature. Administrators can't adjust these limits; Microsoft sets them. The Windows behemoth says it "doesn't publish specific limits because they're subject to change." Microsoft also suggests that hitting a limit "might indicate interest in additional Copilot capabilities." The remedy it proposes for administrators to consider is, conveniently, another license. Users may also be offered an upgrade route – although buying a license themselves depends on whether their organization permits self-service purchases. Microsoft explained: "In most organizations, the limit notification includes an option to upgrade. "Users can select it to request a Microsoft 365 Copilot license from their admin, who can approve or deny requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center. If the organization allows users to buy licenses directly, users might also see an option to purchase a license." Microsoft concluded: "Admins can turn off direct purchases for each product." The rollout began on November 2 for organizations with 2,000 or fewer Microsoft 365 seats and is due to start on November 9 for larger organizations. It also applies only to users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license in commercial tenants. Web, desktop, and mobile apps are all affected. The change could be Microsoft's latest wheeze to turn included Copilot Chat access into paid add-on sales. Users who hit an unpublished ceiling may well start pestering administrators for an upgrade. The alternative is that admins decide tighter controls are preferable to unpredictable feature availability. Not necessarily the sales outcome Microsoft had in mind. ®

articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 sales dropped by 41% from last year due to console's price increase
articles.content: Nintendo Switch 2 sales have dropped 41% in the second fiscal quarter compared to the same quarter last year, as reported by CNBC and as predicted by Kantan Games CEO Serkan Toto at the beginning of June, selling only 2.67 million units from July to September. Nintendo is still sticking to its forecast of 16.5 million units sold by the end of the fiscal quarter, but is under pressure from investors to release more big hits to sell more Switch 2 units to hit its goal. In Japan’s second fiscal quarter running from July 1 to September 30, Nintendo increased the price for the Switch 2 in the US, Canada, and Japan after an initial price hike in Japan earlier this year. Serkan Toto, CEO of Kantan Games Inc., which tracks and analyzes the Japanese game industry, expected that the price increase would lead to a decrease in sales. Despite the prediction coming true, Nintendo is assuring its investors that it would hit its forecast of 16.5 million units sold by March 31, 2027, the end of Japan’s current fiscal year. Toto also stated, “Nintendo’s only real blockbuster this fiscal year is the Ocarina of Time remake. It’s not enough to make investors happy, especially after the device is now as expensive as it is.” The remake, set to release tomorrow, disappointed many fans, with its visuals being uncanny and overly photorealistic, instead of being true to the original art style with updated audiovisuals. The game also seems to have limited offerings to expand on the original Ocarina of Time, even missing the more difficult Master Quest mode, which many veterans were looking forward to. Overall, the remake may not generate as much excitement as Nintendo expects, with fans viewing it as more of a reskin than a release worthy of the hype. This could potentially dampen the Switch 2 sales Nintendo was hoping the remake would drive, but we will have to see how well it performs after its release. It also doesn’t help that Macronix , one of Nintendo’s ROM chip manufacturers, recently stopped ROM chip manufacturing to focus its capacity on high-demand NOR and NAND flash chips for AI data centers, even banking on the memory price hikes for short-term gain. Currently, Nintendo is pressured to release more big games to make the Switch 2 more attractive, with new Pokémon games planned for 2027 — Who knows, maybe Nintendo might cave in and finally accept Palworld onto its platform.
